name: Isolated Congenital Laryngeal Web

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Endoscopic Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Laryngeal Web

criteria.description: Direct visualization of a membranous web across the laryngeal airway by laryngoscopy
No associated syndromic features or other congenital anomalies
Presence of congenital stridor or respiratory distress in neonate or infant
Assessment of vocal cord mobility showing normal or restricted movement without paralysis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Direct laryngoscopic visualization of the laryngeal web with absence of other syndromic anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and confirmed by endoscopic examination; genetic testing is not routinely indicated in isolated cases.

imaging: Direct laryngoscopy demonstrating membranous web across anterior glottis
Flexible or rigid endoscopy confirming extent and thickness of web
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated with isolated cases; genetic testing generally not indicated
other: Pulmonary function tests may show variable airway obstruction in older children
Voice assessment revealing dysphonia or weak phonation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of vascular lesion on laryngoscopy
Narrowing below the vocal cords rather than membranous web

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress or airway obstruction
Failure to thrive due to feeding and respiratory compromise
references: Orphanet: Isolated Congenital Laryngeal Web - ORPHA:2374
Koufman JA, et al. Congenital laryngeal webs: diagnosis and management. Otolaryngol Clin North Am. 1991.
Myer CM 3rd, et al. Congenital laryngeal webs: a review of 20 cases. Ann Otol Rhinol Laryngol. 1994.
